newsitem.title: RWANDA: More than 60 killed in Rwanda in past week.
newsitem.headline: More than 60 killed in Rwanda in past week.

text.p: Gunmen have killed more than 60 people in Rwanda in the past week, state radio and U.N. sources said on Wednesday, identifying many of the victims as recently returned refugees who witnessed the 1994 genocide.
The new wave of killings was reported as Rwanda's government said it had arrested three suspects in connection with the brutal slaying of three Spanish aid workers on Saturday night.

Rwandan radio said on Wednesday unidentified gunmen killed 30 people at Nyamugali commune in Ruhengeri district on Monday night. More than 30 people had also been killed in Rushashi in rural Kigali since January 14, U.N. sources said.
The U.N. human rights office confirmed more than 20 people were killed in Nyamugali on Monday night in rising insecurity in the tiny but violent tea and coffee-growing central African nation.
Rwandan officials said the army reacted to Monday's killings in the northwest by sealing the area and starting a search.
"The army is sealing off the area to chase these people," said Claude Dusaidi, political adviser to Rwandan military strongman and Vice-President Major-General Paul Kagame.
In Rushashi, a total of 32 people were killed between 14th and 18th of this month, the U.N. sources said.
"We had 14 killed on January 14th, 12 on the 17th and six on the 18th of this month," a U.N. source said.
"This information comes from the local authorities. There is a group of people killing returnees and genocide witnesses in this area," the source added.

A series of attacks have been reported this month in Rwanda on survivors of the genocide, apparently aimed at stopping them from testifying at trials of suspects accused of involvement in the slaughter of an estimated 800,000 people.

Hutu militiamen suspected to have returned to Rwanda from Zaire among more than 700,000 refugees last year shot dead three Spanish aid workers from Medicos del Mundo (Doctors of the World) on Saturday night in the northwestern town of Ruhengeri.
"We have three people in custody. They are ex-FAR (former Rwandan government) soldiers," said Dusaidi on Wednesday.
Three Rwandan soldiers were also killed in the attack and an American was shot in one of his legs which was later amputated.
Gunmen stormed a house where the aid workers were staying and demanded their passports before shooting the three Spaniards at close range. The American was shot as he dived under a table.
The killers were said by Rwandan military sources to have belonged to the Hutu Interahamwe militia which played a leading role in the 1994 slaughter before being driven into Zaire by Tutsi rebels.
The bodies of the three Spaniards were flown on Tuesday from the Rwandan capital Kigali to Nairobi, Kenya, where officials said they would be put to a flight on Wednesday to Brussels.
U.N. and other aid agencies reiterated on Tuesday they would not close down their humanitarian programmes in the Ruhengeri and Gisenyi areas of the northwest because of the killings.

Rwanda's genocide was sparked off by the assassination of Hutu military strongman Juvenal Habyarimana in April 1994. Angry Habyarimana supporters took up arms and hunted down Tutsis and moderate Hutus opposed to his junta.

Diplomats at the United Nations in New York said on Tuesday that Algerian diplomat Mohamed Sahnoun, who once headed the U.N. operation in Somalia, would be named as a special representative for the Great Lakes region of Central Africa including Rwanda.
They said he would jointly represent both the United Nations and the Organisation of African Unity.
